newsitem.title: USA: WALL STREET LICKS WOUNDS AFTER BONDS CALL SHOTS.
newsitem.headline: WALL STREET LICKS WOUNDS AFTER BONDS CALL SHOTS.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were in a punch-drunk daze at midday Wednesday, licking their wounds from two ferocious reversals and still vulnerable to more swings in the bond market, analysts said.
"The issues that whipsawed the market today were the economic releases and the bond market," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds.
"We dodged the bullet with the PPI number so I think all focus shifts gear to tomorrow to the CPI," he said.
At midday the Dow was off nearly 19 points at 7942.
Half an hour later, the index was up two points.
A smaller-than-expected rise in July U.S. retail sales prompted a rally in bonds that fizzled just as the Dow surged after its opening.
The loss of steam in the bond market ripped the rug from under stocks, pushing the Dow 160 points lower, but by midday the index had shed most of the losses.
The producer prices index for July, also released today, fell for the seventh consecutive month.
The long bond was up 12/32 to yield 6.64 percent, but two-thirds of the earlier gains were lost.
The Consumer Price Index for July is due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT Thursday. Analysts forecast a rise of 0.2 percent. compared with an increase of 0.1 percent in June.
The slide in the dollar against the mark in Europe was having some effect on stocks as it weighed on bonds, but this was downplayed by analysts.

Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross, said bond prices had been rising on the assumption that the economy would remain relatively slow and interest rates would not go up. "Now we are seeing signs that maybe the economy is a little stronger," he said.
The Consumer Price Index is seen by analysts as more important than the PPI because it is closer to the consumer.
"I think we have seen the highs and the lows for the day, and over the next few days we will see continued volatility and not much progress in either direction," Blumberg said.
The volatility will come from stocks taking their cue from bonds and economic data in the absence of major earnings reports, analysts said.
Nasdaq mirrored the see-sawing on the Big Board and recovered to move 5.16 points higher at 1581.40.

Micron Technologies shed seven points to 43-1/8. Before the open, Merrill Lynch cut the stock's rating and trimmed profit estimates. Other brokers also cut expectations, citing falling prices for memory chips.
But Applied Materials Inc, the biggest manufacturer of chip-making equipment, surged after reporting stronger-than-expected earnings. The stock was up 8-1/2 at 98-3/4.
